title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error visible. The converse is only begun ('Inversement si ... un tel morphisme') and left unproved. It is true under the stated conditions: componentwise iso on normalizations, and marked points going to marked points or nodes; one also needs points that are glued in X' to go to points glued compatibly in X, which holds automatically by continuity of the map on branches.
Implicit hypothesis: σ' must be compatible with σ under the injection A' -> A (glued pairs in X' map to glued pairs in X). The page does not state this, though it is needed for X' -> X to be defined.

ideas.what: Morphisms of combinatorial types (modular graphs) G' -> G: a vertex map preserving genus, injective on half-edges at each vertex, compatible with the edge involution.
ideas.modern_name: étale/immersion-type morphisms of stable graphs (local injections of modular graphs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Graph categories for M̄_{g,n}: Knudsen (clutching), Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Costello, Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification of M̄_{g,ν} by types but not to this graph-morphism formalism

ideas.what: Correspondence between such morphisms of types and finite unramified ('fini net') maps of nodal curves that are isomorphisms on normalized components and send marked points into marked points or singular points.
ideas.modern_name: partial normalization / gluing (clutching) maps; finite unramified covers of nodal curves by components

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins an equivalence between a category of combinatorial types of stable curves, with morphisms allowing repeated components (u_0 non-injective), and finite unramified normalization-preserving maps of curves. This would make the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,ν} functorial for a larger class of graph morphisms than the usual contraction/clutching morphisms. It is unfinished on the page and close to known formalisms, so its novelty is limited.
missed.quote: X' ⟶ X morphisme fini net appliquant I' dans I ⊔ Sing X ... Inversement si ... un tel morphisme
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Morphisms of this kind, which allow components to be duplicated, are closer to graph immersions or coverings than to standard modular-operad morphisms. They are relevant to Hurwitz-type and tropical covering constructions. This is mildly interesting, but largely covered implicitly in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine formalization of graph-type morphisms and the corresponding finite unramified maps of nodal curves. It is standard to specialists and incomplete on the page.
transcription_corrections: The insertion 'sur corps k' is a superscript added above 'ou sa normalisée' and belongs after 'de type G'. Reading: 'Soit X une courbe de type G, sur corps k, ou sa normalisée ...'
The insertion above 'opérant' is unclear ('cisaures[?]'); the sense is 'σ' opérant sur A'_k', possibly with an adverb added.

The end of the struck-out passage reads roughly 'et qui sur les normalisés induit des iso composante par composante' (componentwise isomorphisms on normalizations), rather than '... iso ... compo. invid.'
Last line likely: 'Inversement, si ... un tel morphisme ...' (the converse), left unfinished.
